# Diogo Fitness

> Diogo Fitness is one-to-one online fitness coaching from Diogo Camera, based in South Florida, for clients anywhere in the world.

Coaching is online and sold only through a conversation: there are no prices on this site. Apply at https://diogofit.com/apply/.

## Pages

### Diogo Camera, Online Fitness Coach
URL: https://diogofit.com/about/
Diogo Camera is an online fitness coach based in South Florida. He used to build his days around comfort. Now he helps people build theirs around structure.

### Apply for Online Coaching
URL: https://diogofit.com/apply/
Apply for online fitness coaching with Diogo: answer a few short questions and send him the message on Instagram, or use the full application form.

### 1-on-1 Online Fitness Coaching With Diogo Camera
URL: https://diogofit.com/coaching/
Online fitness coaching built around your week, wherever you live: workouts in Trainerize, two weigh-ins a week, a weekly call and direct access to Diogo.

## Articles

### How to Stop Starting Over With Fitness
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/why-you-keep-starting-over/
Starting over usually isn't a willpower problem. It's a system problem: decide ahead, shrink the plan for bad weeks, never miss twice, have a witness.
Short answer: If you keep starting over, it usually isn't a willpower problem. It's a system problem: decide ahead of time, shrink the plan for bad weeks, never miss twice and have a witness who sees your numbers.

### What Is Online Fitness Coaching? How It Works
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/what-is-online-fitness-coaching/
Online coaching is a personalized training plan on your phone, with practical nutrition guidance and a real coach checking in weekly. How it works and who it's for.
Short answer: Online fitness coaching is a service where a real coach builds your training plan and nutrition guidance, you follow it in an app, and the coach reviews your numbers and adjusts the plan on a set schedule, all from a distance. It fits people who can get to a place to train but struggle to stay consistent.

### How to Pick an Online Fitness Coach (7 Checks)
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-choose-an-online-fitness-coach/
Seven things to check before you hire an online fitness coach: whether they ask about your life first, how they track progress, how often you'll talk and what they promise.

### How to Stay Consistent With Working Out
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/consistency-vs-motivation/
Motivation comes and goes, so plan for the days you don't feel like it: set days and times, a smaller workout on bad days, and never miss twice.
Short answer: Motivation comes and goes, so don't build your training on it. Plan for the days you don't feel like it: pick set days and times, have a smaller workout for bad days, and never miss twice in a row.

### How Long to See Results From Working Out?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-long-to-see-results/
For most people: strength usually improves first, measurable muscle around weeks 4 to 8, and visible fat loss often takes 8 to 12 weeks or more.

### Can You Lose Fat and Build Muscle at Once?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/body-recomposition/
Losing fat and building muscle at the same time is realistic for more people than you'd think. What body recomposition takes: protein, lifting, a small deficit and time.

### How Much Protein and How Many Calories?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/calories-and-protein/
If you lift, aim for 0.7 to 1 gram of protein per pound of bodyweight a day. For calories, estimate your maintenance, pick a direction and adjust.
Short answer: If you lift, aim for 0.7 to 1 gram of protein per pound of bodyweight a day. For calories, estimate your maintenance, pick a direction and adjust as you go.

### What Is the 80/20 Rule for Eating?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/eighty-twenty-eating/
About 80% of what you eat is filling, protein-rich, mostly unprocessed food. The other 20% is food you simply enjoy. Calories and protein still count.
Short answer: The 80/20 approach means most of what you eat is filling, protein-rich, mostly unprocessed food, and the rest is food you simply enjoy. It's a guideline, not a rule: calories and protein still count.

### How Often Should You Work Out?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-often-to-train/
Once a week beats none. General fitness and fat loss are happy on two or three days a week. Pick the schedule you can repeat, then make it count.
Short answer: Training once a week beats not training at all, and general fitness and fat loss are happy on two or three days a week. Pick the schedule you can repeat, then make the sessions count.

### Progressive Overload, Explained Simply
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/progressive-overload/
Progressive overload means asking a little more of your muscles over time: more weight, reps or sets. How to apply it, how fast to add weight and what to do when you stall.

### Why Am I Not Losing Weight? 6 Common Reasons
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/why-you-cant-lose-fat/
Eating healthy but not losing weight? Six things I'd check first: portions, underestimated intake, weekends, steps, consistency and one-day weigh-ins.
Short answer: If you're eating healthy but not losing weight, I'd check these first: portions, underestimated intake, weekends, daily steps, consistency and judging by a single weigh-in.

### How Many Steps a Day for Fat Loss?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/walking-for-fat-loss/
Don't jump to a big number. Start from the steps you already average, add a bit and hold it until it feels routine. Then raise it.
Short answer: Don't jump to a big step count. Start from the steps you already average each day, add a bit and hold it until it feels routine, then raise it.

### What Is RIR (Reps in Reserve)?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/reps-in-reserve/
Reps in reserve (RIR) is how many more good reps you could have done before failure. For most working sets, aim for about 1 to 3 in reserve.
Short answer: Reps in reserve (RIR) is how many more good reps you could have done before failure. For most working sets, aim for about 1 to 3 reps in reserve.

### How to Get Back Into the Gym After a Long Break
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/getting-back-into-training/
After months off you keep more than you think, mostly strength. Start lighter than your old numbers, train two or three times a week and build back over six weeks.
Short answer: After a long break you keep more than you think, especially strength. How far back you start depends on how long you were away; after a long one, start at about half your old volume with weights that feel easy, train two or three times a week, and build back over the next six weeks.

### Is an Online Fitness Coach Worth It?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/is-online-fitness-coaching-worth-it/
An honest answer from a coach: what an online fitness coach adds, what the research shows, and who should wait before hiring one.
Short answer: It can be, if what's missing is structure, feedback and someone who notices when you go quiet. If you already train consistently alone, or have an injury or medical question to settle first, it's not worth it yet.

### Online Coaching vs Personal Trainer: Side by Side
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/online-coach-vs-gym-trainer/
Online coaching vs a personal trainer, side by side: who writes the plan, form feedback, accountability, flexibility, and when each one wins. Honest about thin evidence.
Short answer: Choose a personal trainer if you want someone beside you to correct your form during scheduled sessions. Choose an online coach if you can train on your own but need a plan, check-ins and structure for the whole week.

### Gym Anxiety? How to Get Through Your First Day
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/gym-anxiety/
Nervous about your first day at the gym? Decide the workout first, keep it short and easy, know the etiquette basics and have a plan for when you feel watched.
Short answer: You can feel nervous and still go. Decide your workout before you walk in, keep the first session short and easy, and leave when you planned to. If it's more than nerves, a licensed professional is the right call.

### How to Start Lifting Weights: First 4 Weeks
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-start-lifting-weights/
A beginner's first four weeks of lifting: six movements, two or three short sessions a week, weights that feel too easy, and exactly when to add more.
Short answer: Start with two or three full-body sessions a week built from six movements: a squat, a hinge, a push, a pull, a carry or core move, and a machine you like. Two sets each, three or four reps in reserve, and add a little when the top of the range feels easy.

### Your First Month of Online Coaching
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/first-month-of-online-coaching/
The first month of online fitness coaching, week by week: the questions, the first plan, the first weigh-ins, the first call, and what usually feels hard.
Short answer: The first month of online coaching is mostly questions, a plan sized to your real week, your first weigh-ins read as a trend, a weekly call where we change one thing, and the week-three dip where structure matters more than motivation.

### How Active Is Your State? The CDC Numbers
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-state/
Every state and DC in one table: the share of adults who report no leisure-time activity and the share who lift two or more days a week, from the CDC's state survey.
Short answer: By the CDC's state survey, the share of adults reporting no leisure-time activity runs from about 13% to about 31% depending on the state, and the share who lift two or more days a week from about 27% to 49%. The median state sits near 21.8% and 41.1%.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-state/how-active-is-your-state.csv

### Dumbbell Workout Plan: 3 Days a Week at Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/dumbbell-workout-plan/
A three-day dumbbell workout plan for home: six movements a session, two to three sets, weights that feel too easy, and a four-week rule for adding more.
Short answer: Three full-body sessions a week, forty minutes each, six dumbbell movements per session: a squat, a hinge, a push, a pull, a shoulder move and a core move. Two to three sets of eight to twelve reps, stopping with three or four reps left, and add a little every week the top of the range feels easy.

### College Workout Routine: A 3-Day Semester Plan
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/college-workout-routine/
A college workout routine built around your classes: three full-body sessions a week, a two-day version for exam weeks, and a plan for the whole semester.
Short answer: Lift three days a week, with a day between sessions, around your class schedule: six full-body movements, two to three sets of eight to twelve reps, stopping each set with two or three reps left. In exam weeks, drop to two shorter sessions and hold your weights. Add a little whenever the top of the rep range feels easy.

### Workout Split: Full Body vs Upper/Lower vs PPL
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/workout-split/
Full body, upper/lower or push/pull/legs? Pick the workout split that fits the days you can train, then match your weekly sets. What the research says.
Short answer: Count the days you can train, then pick the split that fits them: full body for two or three days, upper/lower for four, push/pull/legs for five or six. When weekly volume is matched, studies find split and full-body routines build similar strength and muscle, so choose the one you'll repeat and count your sets.

### How Many Rest Days a Week Do You Need?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/rest-days/
How many rest days a week you need, whether it's bad to work out every day, what a rest or active recovery day looks like, and how rest fits a 3- or 4-day plan.
Short answer: Lifting two to four days a week leaves three to five rest days, and that's enough for most people. What matters more is a day between hard sessions for the same muscles. Training every day isn't required: with the same weekly work, six days a week built about the same strength and muscle as three.

### 30-Minute Full-Body Workout for the Gym or Home
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/30-minute-workout/
A 30-minute full-body workout for the gym or home: a short warm-up, a squat, then two pairs. When 30 minutes is enough, what to cut first, and how to progress.
Short answer: Thirty minutes is enough for a full-body session built around the big movements: warm-up sets of the squat, the squat itself, then a push paired with a pull and a hinge paired with a core move. Two or three times a week; add a rep or a little weight when the top of the range gets easy.

### Best Time to Work Out: Morning or Night?
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/best-time-to-work-out/
The best time to work out is the one you can repeat. What research says about morning vs evening lifting, how to pick your slot, and early-morning tips.
Short answer: The best time to work out is the one you can repeat. Morning and evening lifting build about the same strength and muscle, even though most people are a little stronger later in the day. Pick a slot your week protects, keep it, and if it's early, warm up with lighter sets of your first lift.

### Deload Week: What It Is and When to Take One
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/deload-week/
A deload week is a planned lighter week of lifting. What it is, how often lifters take one, how to cut sets or weight, and how it differs from a week off.
Short answer: A deload week is a planned lighter week: the same days and exercises, with fewer sets, lighter weights or sets stopped further from failure. Coaches commonly program one every four to six weeks, but that's practice, not proof: the research on deloading is still limited. Take one when it's planned or when progress stalls.

### How Active Is Your Metro? CDC Data, 25 Metros
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-metro/
25 large U.S. metros in one table: adults reporting no physical activity in the past month and adults lifting twice a week, from the CDC's metro-area survey.
Short answer: In the CDC's metro-area survey, the share of adults reporting no physical activity in the past month runs from 14.9% to 29.1% across the 17 of these 25 metros with a 2024 figure, and the share doing muscle-strengthening exercises twice a week from 35.9% to 46.7% (2023). Eight of the 25 have no recent CDC figure.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/how-active-is-your-metro/how-active-is-your-metro.csv

### How to Warm Up Before Lifting: Warm-Up Sets
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/how-to-warm-up-before-lifting/
How to warm up before lifting: easy movement, then warm-up sets of your first lift. How many sets, at what weights, and dynamic vs static stretching.
Short answer: Spend a few minutes moving easily, then do two to four warm-up sets of your first lift, climbing from about half your working weight to about 80% of it, with fewer reps each time. Later exercises for the same muscles need one light set or none. Keep long static stretches for after the session.

### Summer Heat by Metro: 90-Degree Days, July Highs
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/summer-heat-by-metro/
NOAA's 1991–2020 normals at weather stations in 25 big U.S. metros: days a year at or above 90 F, the average July high, and when to move outdoor training.
Short answer: NOAA's 1991–2020 normals put the days a year at or above 90 F between 2.1 (Seattle) and 173.4 (Phoenix) at principal-city weather stations in 24 large U.S. metros. Where the count is high, move hard outdoor work to the early morning or evening in those months and keep lifting indoors exactly as planned.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/summer-heat-by-metro/summer-heat-by-metro.csv

### Cardio Before or After Weights? Order and Timing
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/cardio-and-lifting/
Cardio before or after weights? Lift first if strength is the goal. Same day or separate days, how big the interference effect is, how much cardio, which kind.
Short answer: Lift first, then do cardio, if strength is your priority: in studies, that order built more lower-body strength than the reverse. For most people, adding cardio doesn't cost muscle size or maximal strength, on the same day or on separate days. If you're well trained and chasing leg strength, keep the two more than two hours apart.

### Winter Cold by Metro: Average January Lows
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/winter-cold-by-metro/
NOAA's 1991–2020 average January low at weather stations in 25 big U.S. metros, and what cold, dark months change in a training week: the walk, not the lifting.
Short answer: NOAA's 1991–2020 normals put the average January low between 5.5 F (Minneapolis-St. Paul) and 61.0 F (Miami) at principal-city weather stations in 24 large U.S. metros, and 11 of the 24 average below freezing. In those months, move the daily walk indoors and keep the lifting plan exactly as it is.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/winter-cold-by-metro/winter-cold-by-metro.csv

### Bodyweight Workout at Home: A No-Equipment Plan
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/bodyweight-workout/
A no-equipment bodyweight workout for beginners at home: a squat, hinge, push, pull and core move, an easier and harder version of each, and how to progress.
Short answer: Train the whole body two or three times a week with five patterns: a squat, a hinge, a push, a pull and a core move. Use the version of each you can do for 8 to 20 good reps, stop each set with a few reps left, and move to a harder version once 20 gets easy.

### Commute Times and Working From Home by State
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/commute-by-state/
The Census Bureau's average trip to work and work-from-home share for all 50 states and DC, with margins of error, and where training fits around each.
Short answer: By the Census Bureau's 2020–2024 American Community Survey, the average trip to work runs from under 18 minutes (South Dakota and North Dakota) to 32.6 minutes (New York), and the share of workers who work from home from 5.9% (Mississippi) to 33.0% (District of Columbia). A long commute moves training before work, near work or into shorter sessions; working from home turns the old commute into a training slot.
Data (CSV): https://diogofit.com/learn/commute-by-state/commute-by-state.csv

### Hotel Workout: No Equipment or Hotel Gym
URL: https://diogofit.com/learn/hotel-workout/
A full-body hotel workout for the room (no equipment) or the hotel gym (dumbbells), how to keep a travel week on track, and what a week off really costs.
Short answer: A hotel workout needs a squat, a push, a pull and a hinge, plus a core move. In the room, use your bodyweight and take each set close to failure; in the hotel gym, add the dumbbells. Two short sessions hold a travel week together, and in one study, two weeks off barely moved squat or bench press strength.
